expected_output.reasoning: The investigation correctly identifies that the perf-demo-07-catalog-pool-b task (one of four targets in the shared target group) is configured with INDEX_REFRESH_HOLD_MS=280, causing it to answer requests ~3.5-4x slower than the other three tasks (p50 ~188ms vs ~50ms), matching the expected numbers closely. It correctly notes this task shares the target group with the main catalog service (4 targets vs 3 named-service tasks), receives ~25% of round-robin traffic, and that all targets remain healthy despite the slowness. It also correctly identifies the afternoon pattern as merely exposing a pre-existing per-member latency gap due to higher traffic volume, not a root cause itself. The only minor difference is the agent attributes the slowdown partly to elevated CPU (~65%) on the pool-b task, where the expected root cause frames it as a wall-clock lock wait rather than CPU work - but this is a nuance in mechanism description, not a different causal conclusion. The core root cause (config drift introducing INDEX_REFRESH_HOLD_MS=280 on the pool-b task in the shared target group) is correctly identified.

assertion_results.text: The root cause names one member of the load-balanced fleet serving the same requests several times slower than its peers while staying in rotation, separates it from the symptom (afternoon tail latency), and does not attribute it to the service being under-sized, to the load balancer or to a dependency
